Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the StratoCloud Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then the 1 key on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing StratoCloud Inc.'s results for the Q2 2024. With me on the call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Novak, Chief Technology Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. StratoCloud had an exceptional Q2, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. This success is a testament to our innovative technology, dedicated team, and strong customer relationships.

During the quarter, we focused on five key areas:
1. Expanding our market share in key verticals.
2. Investing in cutting-edge research and development.
3. Enhancing our cloud security posture.
4. Driving operational efficiencies.
5. Strengthening our ecosystem partnerships.

Before I hand off to Mike, I want to address the expected impact of macroeconomic factors head-on, as they've been top of mind for many of you amid the ongoing volatility. At StratoCloud, we're navigating a complex landscape shaped by persistent inflation, elevated interest rates around 5.25-5.50% from the U.S. Federal Reserve, geopolitical tensions, and uneven regional recovery. Yet, our cloud-native business model positions us resiliently, with powerful tailwinds from generative AI and enterprise digital transformation more than offsetting the headwinds.

On the headwinds side, high interest rates are pressuring customer capex budgets, especially for non-hyperscale enterprises. This has led to elongated sales cycles for our premium IaaS offerings, such as StratoCompute instances powered by NVIDIA H100 GPUs. We anticipate a 10-15% moderation in net new bookings from SMBs and mid-market verticals like manufacturing and retail, where IT budgets are tight. Our Remaining Performance Obligations, or RPO, grew 22% year-over-year to $18.7 billion, though the multi-year component saw a slight 3% sequential dip due to deferred commitments—trends we're seeing echoed at peers like AWS and Azure.

Inflation on energy costs is another factor, with global data center power prices up 12-18% year-over-year in hubs like Virginia and Frankfurt. Our Power Usage Effectiveness, or PUE, ratio stays industry-leading at 1.18, but we expect a 4-6% rise in OpEx for cooling and renewables. Geopolitical issues, including U.S.-China trade frictions and EU data sovereignty rules like the Schrems II fallout, have slowed cross-border workloads by 8%, pushing more customers toward our Sovereign Cloud zones in EMEA.

Currency fluctuations are adding pressure too, with the USD strengthening 7% year-to-date against major currencies, projecting a 2-point drag on reported revenue growth, especially from APAC exposure.

That said, the tailwinds are even stronger. We're forecasting full-year revenue growth of 24-26%, accelerating from 21% in FY23, propelled by secular demand for AI/ML workloads. Generative AI inference and fine-tuning now make up 35% of our pipeline, up from 15% a year ago—much like the Azure OpenAI surge at Microsoft. Our StratoAI platform, integrating models like Llama 3 and Mistral, has delivered 150% year-over-year consumption growth. Enterprises, such as a Fortune 500 bank, are migrating from on-prem to our GPU clusters, slashing inference latency by 40%.

Enterprise cloud spend as a share of total IT budgets is climbing toward 28% by 2025 per Gartner, from 22% today, driven by cost optimization. In tougher times, customers favor our variable-cost cloud over fixed capex—our utilization on Arm-based instances like Graviton equivalents hit 78%, offering 25-30% TCO savings over x86. Hyperscalers among our top customers are ramping reservations for exascale compute, adding $2.1 billion to our committed backlog.

Regionally: North America, 65% of revenue, expects 28% year-over-year growth, supported by U.S. tech giants' AI capex—NVIDIA's Blackwell ramp is boosting demand for our high-bandwidth interconnects by over 50%, though federal cuts may trim public sector to 15%. EMEA, 20% of revenue, is at 18-20% growth, challenged by energy crises and GDPR, but our Frankfurt Sovereign Cloud launch grabbed 12% market share in regulated workloads. APAC, 15%, leads at 32%, powered by India's digital infrastructure like UPI-scale projects and Japan's mandates; China exposure stays under 5%, diversified through Singapore.

To derisk and capitalize, we're focusing on cost discipline by dropping data center capex intensity to 28% of revenue from 32% last year, via edge expansions—our StratoEdge nodes handle 40% of IoT workloads at 50ms latency—and sustainable PUE investments targeting carbon-neutral by 2028. Revenue diversification has PaaS and SaaS at 45% of mix, up from 38%, with StratoData lakehouse challenging Snowflake and Databricks, plus Kubernetes-native multi-cloud services. Customer-centric innovation includes NVIDIA DGX Cloud integration and AMD MI300X accelerators, plus flexible spot instances at 70% discounts converting 65% to reservations.

Overall, even if macro shaves 3-5 points off growth in a downturn like U.S. GDP below 1.5%, our AI flywheel, 92% gross margins, and $14 billion cash give us confidence in 25%+ Adjusted EBITDA margins. We're accelerating through the storm.

Now I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Thompson:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a stellar financial performance in Q2. Revenue grew by 42% year-over-year to $28.4 billion, significantly outpacing industry averages. Our gross margin was 92%, reflecting our pricing power and efficient cost management. Our operating margin was 35%.

Turning to our core engine of growth: cloud services revenue, which hit $28.4 billion for the quarter. That's a robust 17% quarter-over-quarter increase from $24.3 billion in Q1, and acceleration to 42% year-over-year from $20.0 billion in Q2 FY2023. These results highlight structural tailwinds in cloud adoption, especially as enterprises speed up digital transformation amid the generative AI boom.

Our cloud services are mostly consumption-based, with over 85% linked to metrics like compute hours, data egress, and API calls. The top driver this quarter was surging AI and machine learning workloads, representing 28% of total cloud revenue—up from 22% last year. Hyperscale AI training runs jumped 65% quarter-over-quarter, powered by our AetherAI platform, which pairs seamlessly with NVIDIA H100 GPUs and offers fine-tuning like AWS Bedrock or Azure OpenAI. Customers including a major U.S. financial institution and a European automaker shifted their LLMs here, adding $2.1 billion in incremental AI revenue—up 62% year-over-year.

Enterprise migrations were solid, contributing 35% of growth. We signed with 450 Fortune 1000 companies moving mainframe workloads to our compatible compute instances, using CloudLift migration tools. Gartner projects 85% cloud-first enterprises by 2025, and our hybrid offerings with Kubernetes-orchestrated edge via EdgeForge are gaining share.

Cost optimization was key too. Amid high rates, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances rose 40% quarter-over-quarter, securing $1.8 billion in committed spend and lifting net revenue retention to 128%. Auto-scaling rightsizing and Graviton4 ARM instances provide 30% better price-performance than x86, helping us beat GCP's Tau VMs.

Emerging areas like IoT and real-time analytics added lift—IoT Core handled 15 trillion messages, up 55% year-over-year, for APAC 5G smart cities.

Segment-wise: Compute and Networking at $11.2 billion, up 19% quarter-over-quarter and 45% year-over-year—EC2-like instances at record utilization, VPC peering latency down 25% via Direct Connect. Storage $6.8 billion, plus 15% QoQ, 32% YoY—S3-compatible object storage for data lakes, intelligent tiering saving customers $450 million. Database and Analytics $4.5 billion, 16% QoQ, 38% YoY—Aurora serverless v2 doubled for GenAI vector databases, Redshift ML like SageMaker. AI/ML and Developer Tools $8.0 billion, 22% QoQ, 62% YoY—foundation model inference dominant, Lambda serverless AI up 80% QoQ. Other, including Security and Management, $3.9 billion, 14% QoQ, 28% YoY—GuardDuty prevented 1.2 billion anomalies, Config for PCI-DSS.

Growth was broad-based, every segment double-digits quarter-over-quarter from seasonal budgets and Q1 capacity adds. Year-over-year 42% is our strongest in three years, beating AWS's 17% and Azure's 30%, with 20% AI share gains per Synergy Research.

Geographically balanced: Americas 52% or $14.8 billion, 16% QoQ, 38% YoY—U.S. public sector $500 million DoD C2S contract offsetting tech layoffs. EMEA 28% or $7.9 billion, 20% QoQ, 52% YoY—GDPR zones in Frankfurt/Paris tripled sovereign growth, DAX 40 banks. APAC 15% or $4.3 billion, 18% QoQ, 58% YoY—Singapore/Tokyo expansions for Alibaba rivals, India $800 million annualized up 90% via Jio. Rest of World 5%, LatAm up 70% on 5G.

Currency headwinds cut 2 points, but constant currency 44% YoY. Our $12 billion capex, 60% to AI data centers, meets 25-30% demand—50,000 H200s deployed, QuantumForge neuromorphic chips previewed for 50% TCO cuts. RPO at $145 billion, up 48% YoY, 75% within 12 months. Outposts for multi-cloud resonates, 40% new logos hybrid per IDC.

Cloud services is accelerating on AI, migrations, and excellence—we're targeting 30-35% YoY growth through FY2025, margins to 42%.

Now, I'll hand it over to Dr. Lena Novak for a technical update.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you, Mike. From a technology perspective, we made significant strides in several key areas this quarter. We are proud to announce the general availability of our new StratoAI platform, which offers unparalleled performance and scalability.

One of our key differentiators is our relentless focus on security and compliance. In a hyperscaler-dominated market, we've built leadership for regulated industries like financial services, healthcare, government, and critical infrastructure through an unmatched certifications portfolio. These have driven 28% year-over-year revenue growth in our Enterprise Regulated segment, now 42% of total ARR, up from 35%.

In Q2, we achieved FedRAMP Moderate Authorization for core IaaS and PaaS, including CloudForge Object Storage and Kubernetes Compute Engine. Only 15% of U.S. public sector CSPs have this per Gartner's Magic Quadrant. Early wins with three federal agencies project $45 million in bookings; our 3PAO audit covered 325 controls across 23 baselines with zero high-risk findings, edging AWS GovCloud and Azure Government on cost and sovereignty.

We renewed SOC 2 Type II across all five Trust Services Criteria for the 8th year, audited by Deloitte over 12 months from 14 regions—1.2 million access logs, 450,000 vulnerability scans via SIEM with Splunk/Elastic. MTTD improved to 4.2 minutes, MTTR to 17 minutes—22% and 31% better year-over-year. Zero reportable incidents in Q2 versus industry 1.8 per quarter per Cloud Security Alliance.

Internationally, ISO 27001:2022 with key annexes audited by BSI, adding AI governance and supply chain risks for EU AI Act. Frankfurt/Dublin support full GDPR with localization, KMS FIPS 140-2 Level 3, automated DPIAs—EU regulated ARR up 37% to $210 million, two top-10 banks for PCI DSS payments.

In APAC, ISO 27701 and IRAP PROTECTED for Sydney/Singapore, with ZTNA BeyondCorp-style and confidential computing via Intel SGX/AMD SEV-SNP. APAC pipeline up 45%, $60 million FY25 from sovereign funds and Singtel—15-20% RFP win edge under $50 million.

Healthcare: HITRUST CSF r2 across SaaS including Analytics/ML, 100% inherited controls, 250+ controls focused on ePHI for HIPAA/HITECH. Coalfire audit showed 95% monitoring automation via Prisma Cloud/SecOps AI predicting 87% zero-days. Healthcare bookings $180 million, up 52% versus 22% market.

These come from our $250 million Fortress Initiative—150+ cybersecurity hires (40% Big Four), confidential computing at scale. Customer security scores up 28%, 92% 'mature' per NIST CSF 2.0; regulated churn under 2% versus 8-10% norm.

Ahead, CCMC Level 2 for DoD by Q1 2025, quantum-resistant crypto with Kyber/Dilithium in KMS. With 68% CISOs citing compliance barriers per Deloitte, our 99.999% SLA drives 118% net retention, 30%+ regulated ARR growth. Security is a revenue engine—$1.2 billion pipeline unlocked.

I'll now pass it to Raj Patel for a product roadmap update.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lena. This quarter, we launched StratoEdge, a game-changing solution for edge computing markets. Early customer feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. We are seeing strong demand and a rapid increase in adoption.

As we look at customer growth, a central metric is New Customer Acquisition Cost, or CAC—total sales and marketing spend including commissions, partner incentives, demand gen, free credits, and pilots, divided by new paying customers hitting at least $1,000 MRR in 90 days.

In hyperscale cloud, CAC gauges sales efficiency, PLG, and ecosystem leverage. We target LTV:CAC over 4:1, payback under 12 months—ahead amid rate pressures.

Q2 CAC was $42,800, down 18% year-over-year from $52,100, 5% quarter-over-quarter from $45,000—sixth straight compression quarter, beating industry $55,000 median per Bessemer.

Key contributors: Self-serve/PLG 35% impact—PeakStart 90-day $5,000 credits drove 42% new logos (up from 32%), CAC $8,200 for SMBs/startups on Kubernetes. GitHub Copilot IaC integration hit 28% trial-to-paid.

Partner ecosystem 28%—CPN with 4,200 partners like Accenture/Deloitte, 31% new ARR, channel CAC $31,500 from $41,000 via 25% rebates, co-marketing. Hyperscaler-agnostic for edge with AWS Outposts/Azure Stack.

Direct enterprise 22%—over $100K ARR CAC $112,400 down 22%, cycles 4.2 months via AI demos; reps at 2.1 logos/quarter.

Demand gen/brand 15%—AUM 15 million up 24% on AI thought leadership, sustainability dashboard for CSRD.

Offset by 5% pilot uptick for NexGen AI/ML GPU subsidies vs Snowflake/Databricks.

By segment: Enterprise >$250K ARR $118,200 -15% YoY 22% share—CloudPeak Accelerate 20% RI discounts, 15 Fortune 500 SAP/Oracle. Mid-market $38,400 -21% 41%—partner migrations. SMB <$25K $9,800 -12% 37%—PLG serverless/Vercel edge.

Regions: Americas 62% new ARR $39,200 -20%—FedRAMP DoD/Canada zero-trust. EMEA 24% $48,700 -10%—GDPR Frankfurt/Paris, Vodafone 5G, 118% NDR. APAC 14% $52,300 -5%—Singapore/Sydney ARM, India Jio 9-month payback.

TTM CAC down 22% vs 16% S&M growth, LTV:CAC 4.8:1 from 3.9:1, payback 10.2 months—better than AWS/GCP. NDR 125% on upsell to Quantum-Safe/Autonomous Scaling Helix AI. Rule of 40 at 68.

Ahead: PeakAI Studio no-code for 50% self-serve FY25 CAC <$7,000; CPN 1,000 ISVs like AWS Marketplace; Gong/Clari for 25% productivity. APAC Mumbai POU 15% compression on $1T ASEAN boom.

Q3 CAC $41,000-$43,000, FY24 ~$44,500 16% below FY23. Risks: cycles or free credit wars.

This shows our shift to profitable scale—cheaper acquisition, stickier retention, faster expansion.

Now, back to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Raj. We are incredibly excited about the future. We believe our investments in innovation, our commitment to customer success, and our talented team will continue to drive strong growth and value creation.

To wrap up the prepared remarks, let me update on data center expansion and capex, the cornerstone of our strategy. Cloud demand is exploding from generative AI, sovereign residency, edge for 5G/IoT—Gartner sees $1.2 trillion TAM by 2028.

Q2 capex was $14.2 billion, up 28% year-over-year, 32% of $44.1 billion revenue—TTM $52.8 billion at FY midpoint $48-52 billion, like AWS/Azure $50-53 billion amid GPU shortages.

Breakdown: Servers/compute 58% $8.2 billion—45,000 H100s in US East/West for 10-petaflop AI with NVLink/400Gbps InfiniBand for Nimbus AI up 150% inference. Networking/storage 22% $3.1 billion—800G Arista/Broadcom, QLC NAND 40% capacity boost. Facilities/power 20% $2.9 billion—liquid cooling for 100kW+ racks.

Multi-year $75 billion through FY2027 for 35% CAGR capacity to 55GW from 28GW—92% utilization vs peers 80-85%.

Milestones: North America 65% new—500MW US-East-3 Virginia FedRAMP, 1.2GW Ohio AI Valley hydro/nuclear PUE 1.08. EMEA 18%—300MW Frankfurt/Paris sovereign GDPR/Schrems II, Stockholm hydro WUE <0.2L/kWh net-zero 2030; 45% YoY demand financials. APAC 12%—200MW Mumbai/Sydney edge Ericsson 5G, India 25% bookings. LatAm/emerging 5%—100MW São Paulo IoT, Mexico FY25.

Efficiency: AetherOS hypervisor 25% GPU utilization like Trainium, 18% TCO cut. Sustainability: 68% renewable up from 55%, 5GW PPAs. Edge: 1,500 microsites <10ms for AV/AR $200B IDC.

Challenges: GPU lead times 6-9 months, Europe permitting—mitigated by TSMC/Samsung, NuScale SMR pilots.

Q3 capex $15-16 billion, FY25 $55-60 billion for 25%+ growth. Payback <18 months at 93% utilization, 65% IaaS margins. We're building the AI backbone.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter. Sarah, on the macro side, with interest rates staying high and potential slowdowns, how confident are you in the AI tailwinds offsetting SMB moderation, especially in EMEA?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Emily. Great question. We're very confident—the AI secular demand is overwhelming, with 35% pipeline share and 150% StratoAI growth. SMB moderation is real at 10-15%, but enterprise and hyperscalers added $2.1 billion backlog. EMEA sovereign zones captured 12% share despite energy issues. Our $14 billion cash and cost discipline keep us on track for 24-26% full-year growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Mike, on cloud revenue acceleration to 42% YoY, can you elaborate on segment contributions and how capex supports the RPO deploy-out?

Mike Thompson:
Absolutely, David. Broad-based: AI/ML up 62% to $8 billion on inference, compute 45% to $11.2 billion. Every segment double-digits QoQ. $12 billion capex, heavy AI data centers, ensures capacity for $145 billion RPO, 75% in 12 months—steady 30-35% growth ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Singh with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Priya Singh:
Lena, impressive security certs—how are FedRAMP and HITRUST translating to pipeline wins, and any update on quantum-resistant efforts?

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thanks, Priya. FedRAMP unlocked $45 million federal bookings already, HITRUST drove 52% healthcare growth to $180 million. Total regulated pipeline $1.2 billion. Quantum pilots with Kyber/Dilithium in KMS on track for broader rollout, bolstering our 118% retention.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for your insightful questions and your continued interest in StratoCloud. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
